# Relationship Menu

> Relationship Menu (https://relationship-menu.vercel.app) is a free web app for building a "relationship menu": a list of things a relationship could include (communication, affection, commitment, living arrangements, other partners and so on). Each person marks every item Must have, Like to have, Maybe or Off limits; then partners compare answers side by side. There are no accounts and no server database: menus are saved in the browser, and a share link carries the whole menu inside the URL.

Typical use: one person builds a menu (often from a template), sends the template link (items with no answers) to a partner or friend, each fills it in privately, they swap menu links (with answers), and paste both into Compare to see agreements and conflicts.

## Pages

- [Home](https://relationship-menu.vercel.app/): What a relationship menu is, why to use one, how the app works, and what each link is for.
- [New menu](https://relationship-menu.vercel.app/menu): Editor. An empty menu offers templates: Romantic Relationship Starter, Relationship Anarchy Smorgasbord, Polyamory & Open Agreements, Close Friendship, Early Dating, and Co-living & Practical Partnership. Keyboard controls: press ? in the editor.
- [Library](https://relationship-menu.vercel.app/library): Menus saved in this browser, with who each is for, item counts, progress and dates. "Export all menus" saves a backup text file with each menu's title and menu link, made in the browser and never uploaded.
- [Compare](https://relationship-menu.vercel.app/compare): Paste two or more menu links or slugs, press Compare, and filter by Agree, All want, Conflicts, Talk about it, Unanswered or Not on every menu.

## Link format

A menu link is `https://relationship-menu.vercel.app/menu?encoded=<slug>` (URL-encode the slug). A compare link repeats the parameter: `/compare?encoded=<slug1>&encoded=<slug2>`.

A slug is `<title>:<menu>` or `<title>:<menu>:<person>`, where each part is `base64(zlib_deflate(utf8(JSON)))` (standard base64 with padding; the same as pako `deflate` in JavaScript or Python `base64.b64encode(zlib.compress(json.dumps(x).encode()))`).

- `title`: a JSON string, e.g. `"Our menu"`.
- `menu`: a JSON object mapping group name to a list of items: `{"Communication": [{"item": "Daily check-ins", "value": "must-have"}, {"item": "Calling each other pet names"}]}`. `value` is one of `must-have`, `like-to-have`, `maybe`, `off-limits`, or omitted for no answer. An item may also have a `note` (text, up to 280 characters), e.g. `{"item": "Sleeping over", "value": "maybe", "note": "weekends only"}`.
- `person` (optional, menu links only): `{"name": "Sam", "pronouns": "they/them", "note": "..."}`.

A template link is the same menu with every `value` and `note` removed and no `person` part. Items are matched across menus by their text, ignoring case and extra spaces, so menus don't need identical items to be compared.

## Privacy

- Anyone with a menu link can read the answers in it; template links contain no answers.
- Opening a link saves a copy in that browser's Library. It never overwrites a different menu with the same title; the copy gets a new name instead.
- Analytics receive page paths only, never the `encoded` query string.

## Optional

- [Source code](https://github.com/robotoer/relationship-menu): React + TypeScript app. Menus are stored in the browser's localStorage; there is no server.
